transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Skyline Head of ML), Daniel Park (Eng Manager), Sana Ahmed (Procurement), Ben Ortiz (Security)

Summary:
Short renewal + expansion check-in focused on Skyline's upcoming renewal in July, discussion of capacity upgrade to 8 dedicated GPUs, adding EU and AP replicas, contract term options (12 vs 24 months), and security/compliance items required for Private deployment. Agreed on pilot week and action items.

Topics:
- Renewal timeline and pricing posture
- Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscale
- Additional regions and data residency concerns
- Security artifacts (SOC 2, ISO, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot performance tests and success criteria

Action items (captured during call):
- See structured action_items field for owners/due dates

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, quick check that audio sounds good?
[00:05] Marta (Skyline): yeah, sounds good, thanks Alex.
[00:08] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, I'll share screen in a minute, the plan today is to go through renewal options and proposed expansion to dedicated 8-GPU pool plus two region replicas and then talk security artifacts.
[00:20] Daniel (Skyline): Quick note — procurement timeline is tight, Sana's here to confirm we need signed SOW by end of month if possible.
[00:27] Sana (Procurement): yes, timeline is end of month, ideally.
[00:30] Alex: Got it, good to know. Marta, can you remind us of current usage numbers and any big growth forecasts?
[00:37] Marta: Sure, we're currently on Redwood hosted with a mix of gen text endpoints and embeddings. Average sustained QPS around 180, spikes to ~900 for flash sales, monthly active tokens about 1.8b. We're projecting 2.5-3x growth next year depending on feature launches.
[00:55] Priya: Ok that's helpful. For that profile we recommended Dedicated previously, the 8-GPU pool should give predictable throughput and the autoscale burst covers spikes; can you confirm latency targets?
[01:05] Marta: p95 under 350ms for user-facing features, background jobs can be higher.
[01:10] Priya: Good. For quantization and batching profiles we can hit p95 ~220-280ms on A100-equivalent. If you need lower we can tune kernels and route sensitive traffic to a lower-latency tier.
[01:23] Ben (Security): Can you explain the private deployment option again? We have residency and KMS controls to satisfy.
[01:31] Alex: Sure. Private gives you VPC peering and customer-managed control plane; keys can be integrated to your KMS/HSM. We also provide audit logs and per-token retention controls. 
[01:42] Ben: And you have SOC 2 and ISO?
[01:44] Jordan (CSM): Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts after the call; Alex will include a network diagram.
[01:51] Ben: good. Also will need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys — is that supported?
[01:56] Priya: Yes, KMS integration is supported for Private; for Dedicated we can provision tenant-specific keys as well. There was a note earlier about HSM support for certain customers, we can escalate if needed.
[02:06] Daniel: On regions — we want EU and AP capacity for lower latency to customers there. How does replication and failover look?
[02:13] Priya: We can provision additional replica clusters in eu-west-1 and asia-southeast-1. Warm replicas with async KV cache sync is typical; if primary becomes overloaded we can failover but there will be cold-start effects for KV cache. We also support traffic-splitting by region.
[02:28] Marta: And data residency — can we pin customer data to EU only?
[02:32] Alex: Yes, Private can do strict residency; for Hosted / Dedicated we can restrict routing to region and ensure logs stay in-region as per config. We'll include exact config options in the doc.
[02:43] Sana: Pricing question — if we add two regions and upgrade to 8-GPU Dedicated, how much does that move the ARR?
[02:50] Alex: Ballpark: base Dedicated 8-GPU pool is $X/month (we gave placeholder numbers in the deck), adding region replicas has an incremental cost and network egress; we'll send updated quote that lays out 12-month vs 24-month committed pricing and volume discounts.
[03:05] Marta: We're leaning to 24 months if the unit economics make sense.
[03:09] Alex: Understood. Priya, can you talk about the pilot for performance validation?
[03:13] Priya: Yes, recommended pilot is 1 week of production-like traffic in eu-west-1 using your sample traces. We'll run 95th/99th latency, throughput, and token-cost comparisons vs current baseline. We'll capture logs and suggest batching/quantization tweaks.
[03:29] Marta: That sounds good. We'll need to whitelist IPs and provide sample traces — I'll get those to you.
[03:34] Priya: Awesome. One note on transcription / ops: if you use continuous batching heavily you may see cost reductions but latency can be impacted slightly, we'll tune batching windows per route.
[03:46] Daniel: Any known gotchas when migrating from hosted to dedicated for us? 
[03:50] Priya: Main items: model pinning, KV cache priming, and initial traffic ramp to warm caches. Also if you rely on certain streaming behaviors we can preserve those but may require route config. Occasionally customers see tokenization differences across model versions; we run evals to check.
[04:06] Marta: About security reviews — we have external audits. Will Redwood sign a DPA and meet our SOC questionnaire?
[04:12] Alex: Yes, we sign DPAs and we'll work through your questionnaire; Jordan will coordinate with legal.
[04:18] Jordan: I'll take the action to share legal contact and start the questionnaire.
[04:22] Ben: I also want to make sure audit logs include per-request metadata for at least 90 days. Is that a config?
[04:28] Priya: Yes, audit log retention is configurable; for Private deployment you can set retention and export to your SIEM. We'll capture specifics in the security packet.
[04:36] Sana: Procurement needs a breakdown of recurring vs one-time and any exit terms.
[04:41] Alex: We'll include a clean quote and SOW template showing exit clauses; also provide upgrade paths.
[04:47] Marta: On success criteria for renewal — we'll want 10-20% reduction in p95 and predictable cost per 1k tokens, and successful pilot with production load.
[04:58] Priya: We'll size for that.
[05:00] Alex: Ok, next steps recap: we'll send updated pricing, security artifacts, and schedule pilot. Anything else?
[05:07] Marta: No, that's all. Thanks.
[05:09] Alex: Great, thanks everyone.

End transcript.

Call recap / explicit next steps at end of meeting (verbatim):
- Alex: I'll get the updated quote and SOC/ISO docs out by 2026-06-15.
- Priya: I'll run the dedicated 8-GPU benchmark and share results by 2026-06-18.
- Marta: I'll send sample traffic and retention requirements by 2026-06-14.

(Transcription note: occasional mis-hearings, e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash", some brand names imperfect.)
